seoTitle: Connect a Namecheap Domain to Your Wix Website
metaDescription: Learn both the nameserver and manual DNS methods for connecting a Namecheap domain to Wix, plus verification tips and propagation timing.
intro: Connecting a Namecheap domain to a Wix website can be done in two ways: switching to Wix's recommended nameservers for automatic DNS management, or manually pointing individual DNS records if you want to keep control. This guide walks through both approaches.

steps.heading: Add your domain inside Wix
steps.body: Log in to your Wix account and add your Namecheap domain in the domain connection settings so Wix can generate the required DNS values.

steps.heading: Choose the nameserver method
steps.body: For automatic DNS management, update your Namecheap nameservers to Wix's nameservers so Wix handles all records for you.

steps.heading: Or choose the manual pointing method
steps.body: If you prefer to keep DNS control in Namecheap, manually add the specific A record and CNAME Wix provides instead of switching nameservers.

steps.heading: Verify the domain connection
steps.body: Return to Wix and confirm the domain shows as connected, which indicates the DNS changes were applied correctly.

steps.heading: Allow for DNS propagation
steps.body: Give the changes time to propagate before assuming something is wrong if the site doesn't load immediately on the new domain.

faq.question: Should I use the nameserver method or manual DNS method?
faq.answer: The nameserver method is simpler since Wix manages everything automatically, while the manual method suits people who want to keep other DNS records under their own control.

faq.question: Will switching nameservers affect my email?
faq.answer: It can, since nameserver changes hand over all DNS management to Wix, so you'd need to recreate any email-related records there.

faq.question: How long does domain propagation typically take?
faq.answer: It varies by domain and location, ranging from a few minutes to up to 48 hours in some cases.

faq.question: Can I switch methods later if I change my mind?
faq.answer: Yes, you can move from manual DNS pointing to the nameserver method or vice versa if your needs change.
